_comment: Tier-2 for febio::rigid_body#4. Reversing the node order of every quad4 on the block's top contact surface returns the FULL contact travel as interpenetration — as if no <Contact> section existed — while the run still reaches normal termination with exit 0, the same completed-step count as the correct run, and no ERROR or WARNING. The fixture asserts that indistinguishability, which is what makes a reversed surface dangerous. Executed 2026-08-06 on FEBio 4.12.0.86045466d (source build, USE_MKL=OFF). MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): T2_MUTATE=1 neutralises the L.swap / L.drop edits this fixture uses to turn a correct deck into a broken one, so every deck it builds is the correct one and the pitfall is never triggered. Unmutated the fixture still PASSES; mutated it FAILS because the expectation 'facet_winding=reproduced' is no longer printed and the forbidden token 'not_reproduced' appears. Re-verify with `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/Schreibtisch/open-fem-agent/.venv/bin/python source.py` (the mutation branch lives in source.py, so the proof is one command and needs no external harness).
